review.tagline: Python tensor library with GPU support and tape-based autograd for deep learning
review.summary: PyTorch is a Python package that provides NumPy-like tensor computation on CPU or GPU, plus a reverse-mode autograd system for building neural networks imperatively. It ships torch.nn, torch.multiprocessing and a DataLoader, and can be extended in Python or C/C++. GPU backends covered in the README are NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm (Linux only) and Intel GPU.
review.audience: ML researchers and engineers building and training neural networks in Python
strengths: Dynamic graphs execute line by line, so debuggers and stack traces point at user code
Backends for NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm and Intel GPU, plus CPU-only builds
Layers can be written in Python or via a C++ extension API
Pre-built pip/conda binaries, Docker images and Jetson wheels are available
weaknesses: Building from source needs a C++20 compiler, 10 GB disk and 30-60 minutes
ROCm support is Linux only; Windows distributed support is described as a prototype
Source build with CUDA requires matching cuDNN 9.0+, NVTX and compiler versions
Low-level framework only; no model serving or application layer included
needs: Needs Python 3.10+, C++20 compiler (source builds), CUDA/cuDNN, ROCm or Intel GPU stack (optional), Intel MKL
Models: torch.nn modules, CUDA, ROCm, Intel XPU, CPU
